text:
noah: Trying the Windows quickstart (PowerShell) from the repo. First SDK call returns 402 Payment Required even though Console shows a trial credit. Error says "workspace requires billing approval". Anyone hit this before?

tara: Which key type? user key or service account? 402 often means a gating policy.

noah: Using an org-scoped service token `sk-sa-xyz` stored in Windows credential manager. Code is verbatim from quickstart: `client.generate('hi')`

onboard-bot: Auto-check: token_type=service_account, mapped_workspace=W900, billing_status=trial_active, admin_approved=false, admin_email=tara@company.com

tara: Ah — for new orgs we require an admin approval step before service accounts can consume trial credits. It's a safety check so admins opt in to allow headless workloads on trial. UX probably unclear in Console.

noah: I remember clicking through billing but maybe that approval popup didn't show on mobile. How can I approve?

sec: Admins can go to Console -> Settings -> Access -> "Allow service accounts on trial" and toggle approval. Also check Security -> Policy: some tenants require explicit admin approval for any non-interactive key.

noah: Confirmed the admin approval toggle was off. Tara accepted it, retried and got 200. First-run success. :tada:

devex: Thanks — two action items: 1) update Windows quickstart README to mention admin approval for service accounts on new trials, 2) SDK should surface a clearer subcode (e.g., `payment_required:admin_approval_required`) and include a console URL in the error to reduce friction. Filing tickets now.

noah: One extra gotcha: our CI image had REDWOOD_ORG set during build which earlier routed me to an old workspace with no approval. Recommend a short note in quickstarts to avoid baking REDWOOD_ORG.

tara: Agreed. I'll add both notes to the docs PR and we should have the SDK team add an actionable error link.
